input.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
input.rationale: Section 10 provides only a "renewable one-year term" for Maintenance Services and the Agreement contains no renewal mechanics: no renewal term length on renewal, no non-renewal notice window, no vendor renewal reminder, and no cap on maintenance fee uplift (Section 11 simply defers to the Fee Schedule, and no escalation language exists anywhere). The playbook requires renewals be easy to exit and predictably priced, so we add successive twelve-month renewals with a 30-day customer opt-out, a 60-day Garman reminder, and an uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 5%/60-day fallback available. Directionally this is a customer-protective gap-filler; nothing existing benefits us that is removed.

proposal.summary: Add maintenance renewal mechanics: 12-month renewals, 30-day customer opt-out, 60-day vendor reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10 makes the maintenance term "renewable" but is silent on how renewal happens, on the notice we must give and on renewal pricing, so we have added standard mechanics: successive twelve-month renewals, a thirty-day opt-out for us, a sixty-day renewal reminder from Garman, and a renewal uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. If a hard cap is difficult we can accept a 5% ceiling with a sixty-day non-renewal window.

ops.text:
(d) MAINTENANCE TERM AND RENEWAL

The maintenance term shall renew automatically for successive twelve (12) month terms unless Sparkling gives Garman written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) calendar days before the end of the then-current maintenance term. Garman shall notify Sparkling in writing of the upcoming renewal, and of the maintenance fees proposed for the renewal term, at least sixty (60) calendar days before the end of the then-current maintenance term. Maintenance fees for any renewal term shall not exceed the fees for the then-current term by more than the lesser of (i) the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index over the then-current term and (ii) three percent (3%).
